name: Hilton Hawaiian Village
sponsor: Park Hotels & Resorts (NYSE: PK), through Park Intermediate Holdings LLC. Park was spun off from Hilton in January 2017.
sponsorNote: Public REIT: check its latest 10-Q for refinancing plans
whyNow: The ~$1.29B interest-only loan matures Nov 1, 2026, about 5 weeks out. Cash flow held up ($127.7M NCF vs $132.6M at issue), but the 4.20% coupon resets to roughly 6.95%. At an 8.5% hotel cap rate, the balance is about 86% of today's value.
pitch: Senior CMBS or bank execution sizes to about $977M at 65% LTV, leaving a ~$335M gap. Fill it with ~$225M of mezz to 80% CLTV and ~$110M of pref, or have Park pay the loan down with balance-sheet cash. Another option is a 12 to 24 month extension while a full refinancing is marketed. Debt service roughly doubles either way, so the first call should be about how much Park wants to pay down.
points: In-place DSCR is still 2.35×, so cash flow covers today's payments. The question is how much a new lender will fund.
Single-asset SASB demand for trophy resorts is deep. We can run SASB and bank balance-sheet bids side by side.
We'd size mezz and pref separately, so you pick the blend of cost and control.
verify: Whether Park has already signed a refinancing or extension (check its latest 10-Q/8-K).
Whole-loan balance: the $1.29B is estimated from reported debt service.

name: Olympic Tower
sponsor: OMERS (through Oxford Properties Group) and Crown Olympic Partners, an affiliate of Crown Acquisitions.
whyNow: The ~$620M interest-only loan on the Fifth Avenue retail and office tower matures May 2027. Occupancy is 99%, with the NBA leased to 2035, but the 3.95% coupon goes to about 6.95%. At a 7% cap rate the loan is about 74% LTV, above what a senior lender will fund today.
pitch: CMBS or bank senior sizes to about $546M (65% LTV). That leaves an ~$83M gap that mezz covers inside 80% CLTV, so no new equity is required. That's a clean mezz recap for a pension-backed sponsor that prefers not to write a check.
points: DSCR is 2.4× on current cash flow, which should draw several senior bids.
Split the capital: a trophy SASB senior plus a separately marketed mezz tranche.
Start in Q4 to beat the mid-2027 wave of Manhattan maturities.
verify: Whole-loan balance (estimated from debt service).
Current Crown and Oxford ownership split.

name: General Motors Building
sponsor: Boston Properties (now BXP) with 767 LLC and Sungate Fifth Avenue LLC.
whyNow: The ~$2.3B interest-only loan at 3.43% matures June 2027. Leasing is strong (98% occupied, Weil Gotshal to 2034), but debt service would rise roughly 150% at today's rates.
pitch: A $1.8B senior loan at 65% LTV plus ~$414M of mezz and ~$124M of pref covers the payoff. More likely, BXP funds part of it with corporate capital. The mandate is worth pitching as a multi-tranche SASB led by a single arranger.
points: At $2.3B, it's the largest loan in the set.
A structured SASB with a rated mezz can keep the blended cost well under a recap.
Offer to benchmark against unsecured REIT bonds.
verify: BXP's disclosed refinancing plans.
Whole-loan balance (estimated).

name: Del Amo Fashion Center
sponsor: A 50/50 joint venture of Simon Property Group and J.P. Morgan's Strategic Property Fund.
whyNow: The ~$369M loan matures June 2027 with a 15.9% in-place debt yield, among the strongest in the set. Occupancy has slipped from 85% to 75%, and J.C. Penney's lease runs to Dec 2028.
pitch: This is a cash-out refinance. A bank or CMBS senior sizes to about $544M, roughly $170M above the payoff. Pitch a larger loan that returns capital to both JV partners, or a lower-leverage loan at tighter pricing.
points: You can take out ~$170M even at a 6.25%+ coupon.
We'd give lenders a re-leasing plan for the J.C. Penney box.
Both partners are institutions, so one mandate needs only two sign-offs.
verify: J.C. Penney's lease status and dark-store risk.
Whole-loan balance (estimated).

name: Market Street - The Woodlands
sponsor: IMI (Institutional Mall Investors): 99% owned by CalPERS, managed by Miller Capital Advisory.
whyNow: The loan matures June 2027. The trusts hold pieces in WFCM 2017-C38 and MSC 2017-H1, and the whole loan is about $175M (estimated from reported debt service). Latest cash flow is $21.9M at 92% occupancy, a 12.5% debt yield, and H-E-B anchors the center through 2029.
pitch: A bank or CMBS refinance sizes to about $204M, which covers the payoff with roughly $26M of room for cash-out. For a pension-backed owner this is a straightforward refinance, and a lower-leverage loan could price tighter.
points: A grocery-anchored lifestyle center in one of Houston's strongest suburbs.
Life companies and banks will quote tighter spreads than CMBS if leverage stays under 55%.
verify: The whole-loan balance, estimated from reported debt service.
That IMI still holds the asset.

name: The Summit Birmingham
sponsor: JDJ Birmingham Company (Bayer Properties principals) and Institutional Mall Investors (IMI).
whyNow: The ~$211M loan matures Jan 1, 2027, about 3 months out. NCF is up since issue ($19.9M vs $16.9M) at 93% occupancy, but Belk (24% of the space) expires Jan 2028.
pitch: A senior loan sizes to about $185M at 65% LTV. About $29M of mezz closes the gap inside 80% CLTV. Given the timing, run a short-fuse process with a 12-month extension as the fallback.
points: Cash flow is up 18% since the loan was made.
Lenders will focus on the Belk rollover, so bring a backfill plan.
verify: Belk renewal status.
Whether an extension is already being negotiated with the servicer.

name: Headquarters Plaza
sponsor: A Fisher Organization / Olnick Organization joint venture (Brian Fisher and Seth Schochet).
whyNow: The ~$152M loan matures Nov 2027 and has already been modified. Occupancy is down from 92% to 86%. The largest listed tenant's lease ran to July 2025.
pitch: Senior proceeds of about $128M plus ~$27M of mezz cover the payoff. The 14-month runway leaves time to lease up first, or to bring in a pref partner to fund TI and leasing costs.
points: The loan modification suggests the sponsor is already talking to the servicer. Position as the refinance path out.
Regional banks know the Morristown market and are active lenders there.
verify: Terms of the modification.
Current rent roll after the top tenant's 2025 expiration.

name: 245 Park Avenue
sponsor: HNA Group at origination, with 181 West Madison Holding LLC as guarantor.
sponsorNote: Ownership has changed since 2017. Confirm the current sponsor before outreach.
whyNow: The ~$1.08B loan at 3.67% matures June 2027. Annualized NCF ($74.8M) is 32% below underwriting, and at an 8.75% office cap rate the loan exceeds today's value.
pitch: A senior loan sizes to only about $555M at 65% LTV. Mezz and pref cover about $200M more, leaving a ~$344M equity gap. The pitch is a recap: new equity, a discounted payoff, or a structured extension with the special servicer.
points: This is an equity raise with debt attached. Lead with who could provide the new equity.
98% occupied with Société Générale to 2032. Lenders will credit the tenancy, not the value.
verify: Current ownership and sponsor.
Whether the loan is on the servicer watchlist.

name: Moffett Gateway
whyNow: The ~$431M loan at 3.32% matures Apr 2027. The property is 98% leased to Google through 2034, but at an office cap rate the balance is about 113% of value.
pitch: The credit is strong (Google), but valuation limits the proceeds. Senior sizes to ~$248M. Mezz and pref add about $88M, leaving a ~$103M equity gap. Pitch a credit-tenant-lease structure with a longer amortizing loan sized to the lease term, which can beat standard office sizing.
points: Tenant credit gives a lender a basis for a CTL structure that ordinary office sizing misses.
Ask whether Google has expansion or early-termination rights.
verify: Google lease terms (termination options, dark rights).
Whole-loan balance (estimated).

name: Bass Pro & Cabela's Portfolio
sponsor: Starwood Property Trust (NYSE: STWD), an affiliate of Starwood Capital Group.
whyNow: The ~$198M loan across 16 net-leased stores matures Oct 2027. Cash flow is up 41% since underwriting, and DSCR is 3.84×.
pitch: A cash-out refinance. Senior proceeds of about $298M cover the payoff with roughly $97M to spare. Pitch a portfolio CTL or CMBS execution, or a partial sale-leaseback recap.
points: At a 16.8% debt yield, most lenders will want to quote.
Ask whether they want release provisions to sell individual stores later.
verify: Remaining lease terms per store.
STWD's current plans for the portfolio.

name: Marriott Quorum
sponsor: Deason Capital Services, LLC, the nonrecourse guarantor and an indirect owner of the borrower.
whyNow: The $53.7M amortizing loan matures July 2027. Amortization has paid it down, so a refinance at today's rates barely raises the payment (−9% on this stack), even at 65% occupancy.
pitch: CMBS senior at about $53M nearly covers the payoff. A small ~$1.5M mezz piece, or a modest paydown, closes it. This is a fast refinance for a family-office owner.
points: The loan has been modified before. Frame this as a refinance that avoids a second modification.
The in-place 12.9% debt yield clears every lender's hurdle.
verify: Why the loan was modified.
